segments.text: [soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Settle into a stable position and choose one place where breathing is easy to feel. This will be your single star.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Imagine a small telescope turning toward that sensation: nostrils, chest, belly, or another clear point.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Follow one inhale from beginning to end... then one exhale. Let the telescope remain light in your hands.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Attention will discover other constellations: plans, sounds, memories, and interesting mistakes. Notice where it went.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Name the distraction softly if useful... thinking... hearing... feeling... then turn back to the chosen star.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [reassuringly] The return is the exercise. Wandering does not cancel the meditation; it creates another repetition.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Stay with three natural breaths... one... two... three... and begin again whenever counting is lost.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Notice the exact instant an inhale appears and the instant it becomes an exhale.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Let effort soften. Clear focus can be interested and awake without becoming narrow or severe.
[soft, slow, warm voice] For a little longer, keep choosing the same star. Each return polishes the lens.
[soft, slow, warm voice] Now widen attention to include the whole breathing body while the original point remains somewhere within it.
[soft, slow, warm voice] [softly] Open your eyes when ready. Carry the skill of returning, not a demand to remain perfectly fixed.
